proposals.title: BC-07's 'generated by' narration exemption, even after E20's per-candidate symbol_names widening, still rejects a true technical claim phrased as 'generated by <plural noun phrase>' with no leading 'the'/'this' and no single noun matching a real symbol - a THIRD distinct false-positive shape in one session (E20: fixed noun outside the list; PGPY-03, concurrent, Page-Python: a morphological variant of a real symbol name; this: no symbol-shaped noun at all)
files: src/repository_presenter/components/readme/validation/registry.py:334-347 (_generated_by_pattern - the exemption's own regex, unchanged by this proposal's own scope, offered as the site whichever fix lands)
proposals.defect: content_units.json's own authored text (api_reference, type:public_symbol:aspose_html.dom.uievent): 'The UIEvent class represents events that are generated by user interactions with the user interface.' The real docstring (runs/clones/.../src/aspose_html/dom/_event.py:369, read directly): 'Base class for user-interface events (WHATWG UI Events section 5.1).' - a true, verified paraphrase (UIEvent objects ARE generated by user interaction, per WHATWG); the exact bigram 'generated by' was never in the source docstring, the same 'never in the source text to begin with' shape the check's own code comment (registry.py:322-330) already names as the reason no inherited-prose/docstring exemption can reach this class. Confirmed programmatically: with this run's real 248-entry symbol_names set loaded, narration_patterns()['generated by'].search() returns True for this sentence and False for all three of E20's own tokenizer/tree-builder sentences - the fix works exactly as designed for its own targeted shape and this is a genuinely different one.
proposals.why_e20_and_pgpy_03_do_not_reach_it: E20 widens the exemption's noun set to include any exact SUPPORTED public_symbol short name; PGPY-03 (concurrent, this session) proposes extending that to a stem/suffix-stripped match for a morphological variant of a real symbol name (clipping/clip). Neither helps here: the phrase following 'generated by' is 'user interactions with the user interface' - no word in it is a real symbol, a stem of one, or a suffix of one. The claim is true and verified against the docstring's own meaning, not against any single citable noun.
not_proposed: widening the exemption to admit any noun (would readmit genuine self-referential document-generation narration, the class this check exists to catch)
a semantic/similarity check comparing the claim's meaning against the docstring's meaning (out of reach for a deterministic check, rule 13/14)
a fix to this exact sentence alone (a hand-fitted single-instance patch, rejected for the same reason item 41/E9's own text rejected narrowing to one repository's shape)
options_for_the_primary_not_chosen_here: Invert the check's own design: block a fixed, curated list of genuinely self-referential continuations ('generated by this/the tool/pipeline/process/document/readme/library-that-produced-this-file') rather than allowlisting safe nouns - the allowlist shape is what has now produced three distinct false positives in one session (E20, PGPY-03, this one); a blocklist of the actual narration shapes this check was written to catch would need zero widening for any future true technical claim, symbol-shaped or not.

Leave the allowlist shape but widen it a third time (e.g. admit any noun when the surrounding sentence's OTHER content is independently citable to a SUPPORTED fact via BC-04's own binding) - narrower in spirit but couples two currently-independent checks (BC-04, BC-07), a bigger design change than either prior widening.
proposals.corroboration: docs/DECISION_LOG.md, 2026-09-17 (`date` checked against commit 250d5cb's own timestamp), pgpy/LANE-E-13's PGPY-03 entry - an independent one-off worker, same session, same G4-W17 arrival list, found a second distinct 'generated by' false positive on a different repository within roughly the same hour. Two independent measurements of the same check's fragility in one session is evidence this is a real, recurring class, not a one-repository curiosity.
